title: Trump dismissively quips about voters Republicans are pinning their midterm hopes on | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

It’s been more than 10 years since President Donald Trumpquipped, “I could stand in the middle of Fifth Avenue and shoot somebody, and I wouldn’t lose voters.”

His baseisn’t nearly so devotedto him these days. But he still returned to the theme this weekend during one of his many recent stops indeep-red territorywhere Republicans hope he’ll turn out the base for the November midterms.

“When you stand up here, it’s just likethelove,” Trump said at a rally in Tennessee. “I could say the stupidest things, and you clap. ‘Oh, I love you so.’”

Both comments were couched as jokes, but both also pointed to a perception that Trump is happy to feed: that his base is almost cultishly devoted to him — as if they are unthinking automatons.

A number of former Trump associates and advisers have said these kinds of commentsbetray a certain contemptthat Trump has for his voters.

And over the years, he has assembled a lengthy volume of comments that could be understood to be similarly dismissive of the base voters who Republicans are pinning their midterm hopes on.

Let’s recap.

Before Trump’s “Fifth Avenue” comment, he tried out a different version.

“One of the things that came out in the one poll — nobody’s ever leaving me,” he said in New Hampshire in 2016, according toNBC News. “I could be the worst person in the world, they’re not leaving.”

Trump said that even if he did “some really inappropriate things, my people stay.”

“I have the most loyal people — did you ever see that?” Trump said in Sioux Center, Iowa, adding: “I could stand in the middle of Fifth Avenue and shoot somebody, and I wouldn’t lose voters.”

He added: “It’s, like, incredible.”

“Even the really dishonest press says Trump’s people are the most incredible,” hesaid in Sparks, Nevada, just before the state’s caucuses.

“I mean I had already 68% would not leave under any circumstances,” he added. “I think that means murder. I think it means anything.”

After winning the caucuses, Trump pointed to his superior polling numbers among voters with less formal education, which has been one of his most loyal demographics over the years.

But he rather provocatively called them the “poorly educated” — repeatedly.

“We won with young. We won with old. We won with highly educated. We won with poorly educated,” Trump said, adding: “I love the poorly educated.”

In making an appeal to Black voters, Trump offered a pretty dismal review of their conditions.

“Look, what do you have to lose?” hesaid in Michigan. “You live in your poverty, your schools are no good, you have no jobs, 58% of your youth is unemployed. What the hell do you have to lose?”

As CNN’s Kevin Liptak noted late in the 2020 campaign, Trump’s pitch to voters often included sayinghe wouldn’t have visited their localesif he didn’t have to. He often pointed to the freezing weather.

“Before the plague [Covid] came in, I had it made. I wasn’t coming to Erie,” Trump said in Pennsylvania. “I mean, I have to be honest: There’s no way I was coming.”

In another jokey comment, Trump told people assembled in stifling heat in Las Vegas that he needed them to live so they could deliver for him at the ballot box.

“Do you feel the breeze? ’Cause I don’t want anybody going on me,” Trump said. “We need every voter. I don’t care about you; I just want your vote. I don’t care.”

A joke, sure. The crowd laughed. But six rallygoerswere hospitalizedfor heat-related illness.

“Their new SCAM is what we will forever call the Jeffrey Epstein Hoax, and my PAST supporters have bought into this ‘bullshit,’ hook, line, and sinker,” Trumpwrote on social mediaabout the push to release more documents related to Jeffrey Epstein. “They haven’t learned their lesson, and probably never will, even after being conned by the Lunatic Left for 8 long years.”

Trump called these people “weaklings” who “do the Democrats work.”

(Left unsaid: The fact that many of those who had pushed this story before he returned to office were his own high-profile supporters. That included some who went on to serve in major roles, such as FBI Director Kash Patel.)

“When you stand up here, it’s just likethelove,” Trump said in Tennessee. “I could say the stupidest things, and you clap. ‘Oh, I love you so.’ It’s true.”

After some laughter, the president assured that isn’t what he actually does.

“But we don’t say the stupidest things,” he said. “We say things of common sense.”
